subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default subagent tool-inactivity recovery, and if so what thresholds, activity signal, kill semantics, and parent/channel notification contract should it use?
rationale: The source confirms the capability is missing, but the requested behavior adds default runtime policy and config that can affect existing multi-agent workflows, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Design bounded core recovery
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved watchdog that uses explicit tool/run activity, reuses existing timeout and kill primitives, and documents conservative defaults plus upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer to broader activity/watchdog work
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on the sessions.activity and watchdog-alert issues so recovery policy is designed after the shared activity model lands.

options.title: Limit scope to manual recovery
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge/kill yet and instead prioritize the model-facing kill/reap-stale escape hatch for stuck children.

recommendation.title: Design bounded core recovery
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved watchdog that uses explicit tool/run activity, reuses existing timeout and kill primitives, and documents conservative defaults plus upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent registry/spawn/control history makes this the strongest available owner signal for the recovery policy decision.
